subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw change the default host filesystem boundary for multi-agent runs, add explicit per-agent filesystem roots, or keep current trusted-host defaults with opt-in sandbox/workspaceOnly policy?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves unrestricted host read/write/edit when `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is unset, while docs and SECURITY.md describe this as a trusted-operator default; changing it is a security/defaults and compatibility decision.

options.title: Harden default multi-agent filesystem boundary
options.body: Make non-main or configured multi-agent host tools workspace-contained by default, with documented opt-out and doctor/setup guidance for trusted-host workflows.

options.title: Add explicit filesystem roots policy
options.body: Keep legacy default behavior but add a maintainer-approved roots/allowlist policy for agents that need MCP-style filesystem scoping.

options.title: Keep opt-in sandbox/workspaceOnly only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and improve docs/setup prompts so users select sandbox or `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` for this deployment shape.

recommendation.title: Harden default multi-agent filesystem boundary
recommendation.body: Make non-main or configured multi-agent host tools workspace-contained by default, with documented opt-out and doctor/setup guidance for trusted-host workflows.
